Broadband radar cross section reduction by in-plane integration of scattering metasurfaces and magnetic absorbing materials Wei Li a, Yazhong Zhang a, Tianlong Wu a, Jie Cao a, Zhihong Chen a,b, Jianguo Guan a,* a State Key Lab of Advanced Technology for Materials Synthesis and Pro c essing, International School of Materials Science and Engineering, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan, 430070, China b School of Science, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan, 430070, China Abstract: An in-plane hybrid design is proposed to achieve broadband radar cross section (RCS) reduction based on the integration of a diffusion scattering electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) metasurface and a magnetic absorbing material (MAM) at a thin thickness (d)
As a result, the as-designed hybrid metasurface show in both simulation and experiment an unprecedented broadband RCS reduction of 6 dB in the frequency range of 5-34 GHz with d of only 2 mm
On the other hand, metamaterial absorbers (MMAs) have advantages of flexible design, strong absorption, thin thickness and light weight [1-4]

But they still suffer from narrow working bands owing to the resonance absorption 1 mechanisms [5-7] after considerable progresses are made in broadening the absorption bandwidth of MMAs typically by integrating multiple unit cells with diverse sizes or various geometries [8-12]
The hybrid design of MMAs and MAMs has also been proven to be somewhat effective in bandwidth extension [13-16]
Nevertheless, the so far developed MMAs or MAMs all follow the restriction of bandwidth thickness ratio in absorption mechanism [17]
Recently, metasurfaces made of electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) structures are extensively investigated and considered more promising in broadband RCS reduction [18, 19]
They reduce RCS by redirecting the scattered electromagnetic waves to non-critical directions rather than suppressing them by absorbing like MAMs or MMAs [20]
The essence of scattering redirection by EBG metasurfaces is the anomalous reflection based on the phase manipulation of EBG unit cells [21-25] and the generalized Snell’s law [26, 27]

Since the phase of reflected waves can be well designed in a broadband range using the concept of metasurface [28-30], the RCS reduction bandwidth of the metasurface can be broadband rather than narrow-band like MMAs

A simple implementation of the RCS reduction metasurface is to arrange two kinds of unit cells with destructive phase difference of 180  37 in a chessboard like manner [22], mimicking a diffuse reflection surface

In this work, we propose a strategy to achieve ultra-broadband RCS reduction with a small thickness (d) by taking advantages of the absorption of MAM and the scattering redirection of EBG metasurface, as well as their synergistic effect
Our results promote more hybrid metasurfaces with broadband RCS reduction and improve the hybrid design of multiple materials with distinct mechanisms
